newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-T-bond pulls back, confirms Thurs reversal.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-T-bond pulls back, confirms Thurs reversal.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures continued their retreat from Thursday's seven-month high, in what some said could be a preliminary sign of topping action.
September reached a new seven-month peak Thursday at 115-2/32 but fell to a new daily low of 114-17/32 and closed just above there, a sign of technical failure at the high.
On Friday, September seemed to confirm the reversal and fell through support at 114-8/32 to reach 114-01/32.
"We had a reversal top yesterday and that's the first sign that we could be topping out," said Jim Hyercyzk, technical analyst with JAH Research and Trading.
"Last week's close was 114-4/32 and if we close below that, it'll be an even stronger signal that we're topping," Hyercyzk said.

Some traders and analysts said Thursday's rejection of 115-02/32 and Friday's weakness did not mean a change in trend, only a pre-weekend test of support. Hyercyzk said the topping action would not turn into a full-fledged change in trend until support at much lower levels was breached.
"The market doesn't change trend until 110-23/32 is broken, but there is a strong indication the market is topping out," he said.
Tim Ransford, a technical analyst with Dean Witter, said the market had been set up for a pullback, and noted that Friday's selloff was quite orderly.
"I think there's a good chance we pull right out of this," he said. "It's a very recoverable situation."
In the last hour of futures trading, September T-bonds were several ticks off their session low.

Ransford called 114-00 to 114-05 the third of three near-term supports. He said the price action from the 114-01/32 session low was a lot like the reaction from the 115-02/32 weekly high, orderly and not severe.
That combination could allow the market to consolidate or test stiff resistance in the 115-00 handle, he said.
"This is barely 10 percent of the 105-30/32 to 115-2/32 rally," Ransford said.
